grh_c83e900e54a8c49bc524.title: Who's Who
paragraphs: Aging playwright James Markham, increasingly isolated since his wife's death and a string of failed plays, agrees to help young novelist Toni adapt her book That Festive Summer for Broadway. Their collaboration becomes a clash over generations, love and the meaning of the story, and a rehearsal of a love scene briefly blurs the difference between acting and genuine feeling. Toni later learns from veteran actress Margaret Mason that Markham's supposedly busy social life is largely a pose. After another quarrel Toni leaves, while Markham finishes a draft that adds a deeply felt suicide scene for the novel's older father. Toni, her boyfriend Al and Margaret fear Markham may be acting out the scene and rush to his apartment, only to discover that the apparent gunshot was a champagne cork and that he is drunk but alive. Toni returns to the play determined to replace its despair with life, she and Al reconcile, and Markham himself reaches toward a new beginning with Margaret.

grh_c8d60c9cdce0f41a75c3.title: The Old Boy
paragraphs: Professor Charles Grayson is horrified when his newborn son begins growing at an impossible rate. Remembering an earlier accident involving radiation from a cyclotron, Charles concludes that his exposure somehow altered the genes passed to the child. He hides the boy from his wife Ellen and from outsiders as the child races through infancy, childhood, adulthood and old age in a matter of days. By roughly the eighteenth day the son is already an old man, weak and near the end of his life. Ellen finally discovers him, accepts that he is their child, and brings him back into the house. Two days later he dies peacefully in his mother's arms, having lived an entire lifetime in only a few weeks.
